children: Ukraine’s current account posted a deficit of USD 0.1 billion in July 2026, the smallest since June 2020 and down sharply from a USD 4.2 billion deficit recorded in the same month a year earlier.

The improvement was largely driven by a sharp increase in the secondary income surplus, which surged to USD 6.7 billion from USD 1.2 billion, while the primary income deficit narrowed to USD 0.1 billion from USD 0.2 billion.
Meanwhile, the goods account shortfall widened to USD 6.0 billion from USD 4.6 billion, as goods imports rose 12.1% to USD 8.8 billion while exports fell 6.4% to USD 2.9 billion.
The services account gap also expanded to USD 0.7 billion from USD 0.6 billion.
Overall, Ukraine’s current account deficit for January-July narrowed to USD 11.4 billion from USD 20.6 billion in the same period of 2025.
Looking ahead, the central bank expects the current account deficit to reach USD 39.7 billion in 2026.

title: Ukraine Current Account Gap Smallest in 6 Years
